topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: The defocused reflector gain loss impacts link budget margins for Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) compared to conventional designs by increasing spillover loss and noise pickup, degrading SNR and requiring a larger SNR margin in the link budget. This necessitates a careful balance between gain, beamwidth, and interference to maintain optimal performance. Optimizing the reflector surface and feed array together can mitigate the increased spillover loss and noise pickup in defocused reflectors, thereby reducing the required SNR margin by up to 6 dB. This approach balances gain, beamwidth, and interference, improving overall system efficiency and reducing the need for more sophisticated error correction.
